chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Sayyari, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Jamil ibn Durraj who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (AS), 'Are there oceans in the sky/heaven?'

He replied, 'Yes.' My father informed me, from his father, from his grandfather (AS), who said: The Messenger of Allah (SAWW) said: 'Verily, in the seven heavens there are oceans, the depth of one of them is a journey of five hundred years. In them are angels standing in service since Allah created them, and the water reaches their knees. There is not an angel among them but that he has one thousand and four hundred wings. On each wing are four faces. On each face are four tongues. There is no wing, face, tongue, or mouth in them but that it glorifies Allah, the Mighty and High, with a glorification that does not resemble the type of the other.'

key_terms.أَلْفٌ وَأَرْبَعُمِائَةِ جَنَاحٍ: one thousand and four hundred wings

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the angels and oceans in the seven heavens according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to illustrate the vastness of Allah’s creation, linking the physical cosmology of the heavens with the spiritual reality of angelic worship. The detailed description of angels' unique modes of glorification underscores the Shia emphasis on the diversity of divine signs (ayat) in the universe, reinforcing the concept that all creation, regardless of its form, is engaged in continuous tasbih.
